verdict.rationale: Lithic documents its own Card and Account Spend Limits for managing spend velocity. Its Authorization Rules apply at card and account level, cover transaction limits and velocity, and are enforced by the platform without extra infrastructure. The evidence does not detail the specific time windows or count-based velocity rules, so only the core is shown. Missing for 10: explicit daily/monthly/all-time window documentation, explicit transaction-count velocity rules, clear per-cardholder (vs. account) scoping, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ops user, I can set spend limits per card and per cardholder — amount caps over daily, monthly, or all-time windows, and transaction-count velocity rules — enforced by the platform, not my code

citations.quote: Lithic's Card and Account Spend Limits provide basic controls that help customers manage spend velocity.
Rules can be applied at three entity levels: Program level: across the entire card program, Account level: to specific accounts, Card level: to specific cards
Configure Authorization Rules controlling merchant categories, transaction limits, and velocity
you can enforce business-specific authorization logic at the program, account, or card level, without managing additional infrastructure.
